answer.short: $110^{\circ}+70^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$, so the co-interior angles sum to $180^{\circ}$ and $AB\parallel DC$.
answer.worked:

The co-interior angles sum to $180^{\circ}$, so $AB$ is parallel to $DC$ by the converse of the co-interior angle property.

answer.worked: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so $\angle AEB=90^\circ$.

The diagonals bisect each other.
$$\begin{align*}AE&=30\div2=15\text{ cm}\\BE&=16\div2=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

$\triangle AEB$ is right-angled at $E$ and $AB$ is its hypotenuse. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}AB^2&=15^2+8^2\\AB^2&=225+64\\AB^2&=289\\AB&=17\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Determine the size of the unknown angle in each quadrilateral.

answer.worked:
The $230^\circ$ reflex angle is an interior angle. The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+45+35+230&=360\\a+310&=360\\a&=50\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $a=50^\circ$.

The $130^\circ$ angle is outside the quadrilateral, so the interior angle at that vertex is $360-130=230^\circ$. The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+45+35+230&=360\\a+310&=360\\a&=50\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $a=50^\circ$.

The $(2a+30)^\circ$ angle is outside the quadrilateral, so the interior angle at that vertex is $360-(2a+30)=330-2a$. The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+45+35+(330-2a)&=360\\410-a&=360\\a&=50\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $a=50^\circ$.

content.prompt: Show these properties, using full reasoning.

answer.short: $\angle BXD=100^{\circ}$ and $\angle XDB=40^{\circ}=\angle XBD$, so $XB=XD$ and $\triangle BXD$ is isosceles.
answer.worked:
Angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AXC&=180^{\circ}-50^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\\\angle AXC&=100^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
$\angle BXD=100^{\circ}$ (vertically opposite angles).
$$\begin{align*}\angle XDB&=180^{\circ}-100^{\circ}-40^{\circ}\\\angle XDB&=40^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of a triangle. Then $\angle XDB=\angle XBD$, so the sides opposite them are equal: $XB=XD$. Therefore $\triangle BXD$ is isosceles.

answer.short: $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=\angle BAC=60^{\circ}$, so $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral.
answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ADB&=180^{\circ}-85^{\circ}\\\angle ADB&=95^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle ABD$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=180^{\circ}-25^{\circ}-95^{\circ}\\\angle ABC&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle ADC$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^{\circ}-85^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\\\angle ACB&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Adding the angles at $A$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=25^{\circ}+35^{\circ}\\\angle BAC&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
All three angles are equal, so their opposite sides are equal. Therefore $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral.
